1.note: This verse begins a direct quotation from Yahweh, although the text does not say who is speaking. You may wish to indicate that Yahweh is the speaker in your translation, using a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

The terms **see** and **know** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and look very carefully]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [if you can find even one human being]

1.q: אִם יֵ֛שׁ עֹשֶׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֱמוּנָ֑ה
1.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **justice** and **truth**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [if there is one who acts justly, who seeks to be truthful]

Here, **her** represents the people who live in Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [then I will forgive the people who live there]

2.note: Following the custom of the culture, the people are swearing an oath and guaranteeing it by something that they hold sacred, the life of Yahweh. Use a natural way in your language to express an oath. Alternate translation: [I swear by the living Yahweh]

3.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to affirm that Yahweh looks for honesty in his people. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, your eyes are surely looking for honesty!]

These words begin a direct quotation from Jeremiah, who is now speaking to Yahweh, although the text does not say that the speaker has changed. You may wish to indicate that in your translation, using a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.
Here, **your eyes** represents what you look for and approve. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your desires]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of Yahweh punishing the people as if he had physically **struck them**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You brought punishment on them]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **tremble**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [but they remain unmoved]

Jeremiah says **You have completely defeated them** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means that Yahweh punished the people severely, not that he destroyed all of them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [You have punished them severely]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **discipline**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [they refuse to be corrected]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of the people as if their **faces** were harder than **rock**, meaning that they stubbornly refuse to change. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They stubbornly resist you]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of the people repenting and coming back to Yahweh as if that meant to **return** to a place. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they refuse to repent]

4.q: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָדְעוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵי⁠הֶֽם
4.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [for they do not know the way of Yahweh, and they do not know the ordinance of their God]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of the conduct that Yahweh requires as if it were a **way** that people walk along. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [how Yahweh wants people to live]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **ordinance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what their God commands them to do]

5.note: Jeremiah is using the adjective **great** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the important people]

5.q: אַ֣ךְ הֵ֤מָּה יַחְדָּו֙ שָׁ֣בְרוּ עֹ֔ל נִתְּק֖וּ מוֹסֵרֽוֹת
5.note: Here Jeremiah is speaking of the people refusing to submit to Yahweh as if his authority were a **yoke** and **fetters** that they had thrown off. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But they all alike refused to submit to Yahweh’s authority; they rejected his commands]

The pronoun **they** refers to **the great ones**, the leaders to whom Jeremiah said he would go and speak. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But those leaders together broke the yoke]

6.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [That is why]

6.q: הִכָּ֨⁠ם אַרְיֵ֜ה מִ⁠יַּ֗עַר זְאֵ֤ב עֲרָבוֹת֙ יְשָׁדְדֵ֔⁠ם נָמֵ֤ר שֹׁקֵד֙ עַל עָ֣רֵי⁠הֶ֔ם
6.note: Here Jeremiah is speaking of the enemies who will attack the people as if they were a **lion**, a **wolf**, and a **leopard** hunting their prey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [enemies as fierce as a lion from the forest will strike them down; enemies as fierce as a wolf of the deserts will devastate them; enemies as fierce as a leopard watch over their cities]

The expression **will be torn apart** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the wild animals will tear apart all who go out from there]

These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [because they have rebelled against him again and again]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **transgressions** and **apostasies**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [the ways they rebel increase and the times they turn away are many]

7.note: Yahweh is using the question form to declare that he will not forgive the people for what they have done. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For this, I certainly cannot forgive you!]
The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing the city of Jerusalem, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here Yahweh is speaking of the city of Jerusalem as if it were a mother and of the people who live there as if they were her **sons**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The people who live in Jerusalem have abandoned me]

The implication is that the **not-gods** by whom the people swear are idols, which are not really gods at all. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and have sworn oaths by idols, which are not really gods at all]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if unfaithfulness to him were **adultery** and as if worshiping other gods were assembling **to the house of the prostitute**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they were unfaithful to me and gathered at the shrines of other gods]

8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the men of Judah as if they were **well-fed, lusty stallions**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They had strong, uncontrolled sexual desires]

Yahweh is referring to sexual desire in a polite way by using the phrase **neighing to the wife of his neighbor**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [Each man lusting after the wife of his neighbor]

9.q: הַֽ⁠עַל אֵ֥לֶּה לוֹא אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם יְהֹוָ֑ה וְ⁠אִם֙ בְּ⁠ג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר כָּ⁠זֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁ⁠י
9.note: Yahweh is using the question form twice to declare that he will certainly punish this people for what they have done. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [I will certainly punish because of these! … Or even against a nation that is like this, I will certainly avenge myself!]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **punish**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [Should I certainly punish because of these]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **avenge**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [should I certainly avenge myself]

10.note: The term **terraces** describes level strips of ground cut into a hillside on which farmers planted vines. If your readers would not be familiar with what terraces are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [onto her hillside vineyard rows]

10.q: הָסִ֨ירוּ֙ נְטִ֣ישׁוֹתֶ֔י⁠הָ כִּ֛י ל֥וֹא לַ⁠יהוָ֖ה הֵֽמָּה
10.note: The pronoun **they** refers to **her vines**, that is, to the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Remove her vines, for those vines are not Yahweh’s]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people of Judah as if they were **vines** growing in a vineyard. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Remove her people]

The implication is that Yahweh is speaking to the armies of the nations that he will send to attack Judah. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [You armies that I am sending, go up onto her terraces and destroy]

11.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **betraying** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [For they have utterly betrayed me]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the descendants of Israel and of Judah as if each group were a **house**, that is, a family living together. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel and the people of Judah]

12.note: Yahweh is speaking about himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [They have deceived about me]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and they said that he is not]

The people are using **we will not see** as a common expression of the culture to mean “we will not experience.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and we will not experience sword or famine]
Here, **sword** represents war. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and we will not see war]

13.note: Here the people are speaking of the prophets as if they were nothing but **wind**, meaning that what the prophets say is empty and will come to nothing. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the prophets speak only empty words]

The implication is that **the word** means a message from Yahweh. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh’s message is not in them]

The expression **it will be done to them** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [thus God will do to them]

14.note: The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [This is why]

This is the beginning of what Yahweh said. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Yahweh. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord God Almighty said]

14.q: יַ֚עַן דַּבֶּרְ⁠כֶ֔ם אֶת הַ⁠דָּבָ֖ר הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה הִנְ⁠נִ֣י נֹתֵן֩ דְּבָרַ֨⁠י בְּ⁠פִ֜י⁠ךָ לְ⁠אֵ֗שׁ
14.note: The pronoun **you** in the phrase **you have spoken** is plural and refers to the people, while the pronoun **your** in the phrase **your mouth** is singular and refers to Jeremiah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Because you people have spoken this word, behold, I shall place my word in your mouth, Jeremiah, for a fire]

Yahweh is using **behold me** as an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that he was about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [now I am about to place my word in your mouth]
Here, **mouth** represents what a person says. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in what you say]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the message that he will give Jeremiah to speak as if it were a **fire**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I shall place my word in your mouth, and it will be like a fire]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people as if they were **wood** that a fire would burn up. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and this people will be like fuel that the fire burns up, and my word will destroy them]

15.note: Here, **a nation** represents the army of that nation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I shall bring the army of a nation against you from far away]

15.q: גּ֚וֹי לֹא תֵדַ֣ע לְשֹׁנ֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠לֹ֥א תִשְׁמַ֖ע מַה יְדַבֵּֽר
15.note: In this verse, the word **nation** is singular in form, but it refers to all the people of that nation as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “nation.” Alternate translation: [They are people whose language you do not know, and you will not understand what they speak]

Here, **tongue** represents the language that people speak. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [A nation whose language you do not know]

16.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **an open grave** is ready to receive the dead, so the arrows that come from this nation’s **quiver** will bring death to many people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Its quiver is full of arrows that will bring death to many people]

A **quiver** is a case in which a soldier carries arrows. If your readers would not be familiar with what a quiver is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [Its case for carrying arrows]

17.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of enemy soldiers killing the people’s children as if they would **consume** them as food. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They will destroy your sons and your daughters]

Here, **your vine and your fig tree** represents the fruit that those plants produce. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [It will consume the fruit of your vine and your fig tree]

17.q: עָרֵ֣י מִבְצָרֶ֗י⁠ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בָּ⁠הֵ֖נָּה
17.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **cities** that are characterized by **fortification**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [your fortified cities that you trusted in]

18.note: Yahweh is using **make of you a complete end** as a common expression of the culture to mean “destroy you completely.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I shall not destroy you completely]

19.q: כִּ֣י תֹאמְר֔וּ תַּ֣חַת מֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֨ה יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛י⁠נוּ לָ֖⁠נוּ אֶת כָּל אֵ֑לֶּה וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֗ם
19.note: The pronoun **you** in the phrase **when you say** is plural and refers to the people, while in the phrase **then you shall say to them** it is singular and refers to Jeremiah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [when the people say … then you, Jeremiah, shall say to them]

19.q: כִּ֣י תֹאמְר֔וּ תַּ֣חַת מֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֨ה יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛י⁠נוּ לָ֖⁠נוּ אֶת כָּל אֵ֑לֶּה
19.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [when you ask why Yahweh your God has done all these things to you]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **gods** that are characterized by belonging to **a foreigner**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the gods that foreigners worship]

19.q: כֵּ֚ן תַּעַבְד֣וּ זָרִ֔ים בְּ⁠אֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֥א לָ⁠כֶֽם
19.note: The implication is that the people will be taken away from their own country and made to serve foreigners in exile. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [so you will be taken away to a foreign country and forced to serve strangers there]

20.q: הַגִּ֥ידוּ זֹ֖את בְּ⁠בֵ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְ⁠הַשְׁמִיע֥וּ⁠הָ בִ⁠יהוּדָ֖ה לֵ⁠אמֹֽר
20.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh told me to declare to the house of Jacob and announce in Judah that]

21.q: עַ֥ם סָכָ֖ל וְ⁠אֵ֣ין לֵ֑ב עֵינַ֤יִם לָ⁠הֶם֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יִרְא֔וּ אָזְנַ֥יִם לָ⁠הֶ֖ם וְ⁠לֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽעוּ
21.note: Even though Yahweh is addressing these people directly, he speaks about them in the third person as **they**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [foolish people and without heart; you have eyes but do not see; you have ears but do not hear]

Here Yahweh is speaking of understanding as if it were a **heart** that a person could have or lack. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and without understanding]

21.q: עֵינַ֤יִם לָ⁠הֶם֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יִרְא֔וּ אָזְנַ֥יִם לָ⁠הֶ֖ם וְ⁠לֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽעוּ
21.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the people’s refusal to pay attention to him as if they had **eyes** that could not see and **ears** that could not hear. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they can see but refuse to understand; they can hear but refuse to obey]

22.q: הַ⁠אוֹתִ֨⁠י לֹא תִירָ֜אוּ נְאֻם יְהֹוָ֗ה אִ֤ם מִ⁠פָּנַ⁠י֙ לֹ֣א תָחִ֔ילוּ
22.note: Yahweh is using the question form twice to affirm that the people ought to fear him and tremble before him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [You certainly ought to fear me … and you certainly ought to tremble in my presence.]

These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Certainly you should fear me and tremble before me]
Here, **my face** represents my presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from being in my presence]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I made this an eternal decree]

The first pronoun **it** refers to the sea, and the second refers to the **sand** that Yahweh placed as a **border** for the sea. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the sea does not cross over that border]

22.q: וַ⁠יִּֽתְגָּעֲשׁוּ֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יוּכָ֔לוּ וְ⁠הָמ֥וּ גַלָּ֖י⁠ו וְ⁠לֹ֥א יַעַבְרֻֽ⁠נְהוּ
22.note: Yahweh is speaking of the sea and **its waves** as if they were living things that could try to overpower the limit he set for them but could not **prevail**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and even when its waters rise and fall, they still cannot pass that limit, and even when its waves are loud, they still do not cross over it]

23.q: וְ⁠לָ⁠עָ֤ם הַ⁠זֶּה֙ הָיָ֔ה לֵ֖ב סוֹרֵ֣ר וּ⁠מוֹרֶ֑ה סָ֖רוּ וַ⁠יֵּלֵֽכוּ
23.note: Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the sea, which stays within the limit he set for it, and **this people**, who refuse to obey him. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [This people, however, has a stubborn and rebellious heart; unlike the sea, they have turned aside and walked away]

23.q: וְ⁠לָ⁠עָ֤ם הַ⁠זֶּה֙ הָיָ֔ה לֵ֖ב סוֹרֵ֣ר וּ⁠מוֹרֶ֑ה
23.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the people’s will and disposition as if it were a **heart** that could be **stubborn and rebellious**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But this people is stubborn and rebellious in their disposition]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people abandoning him as if they had **turned aside** from a path and **walked away**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They have abandoned me and no longer obey me]

24.q: וְ⁠לֹֽא־אָמְר֣וּ בִ⁠לְבָבָ֗⁠ם נִ֤ירָא נָא֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔י⁠נוּ הַ⁠נֹּתֵ֗ן גֶּ֛שֶׁם ו⁠ירה וּ⁠מַלְק֖וֹשׁ בְּ⁠עִתּ֑⁠וֹ שְׁבֻע֛וֹת חֻקּ֥וֹת קָצִ֖יר יִשְׁמָר־לָֽ⁠נוּ
24.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And they do not say to themselves that they should now fear Yahweh their God, the one who gives the rain—both the early rain and the late rain—in its season, and who keeps the appointed weeks of the harvest for them]

Yahweh is using **say in their hearts** as a common expression of the culture to mean “think to themselves.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they do not think to themselves]

In Israel, **the early rain** fell at the beginning of the growing season and **the late rain** fell near its end. If your readers would not be familiar with these kinds of rain, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [both the autumn rain and the spring rain]

25.q: עֲוֺנוֹתֵי⁠כֶ֖ם הִטּוּ־אֵ֑לֶּה וְ⁠חַטֹּ֣אותֵי⁠כֶ֔ם מָנְע֥וּ הַ⁠טּ֖וֹב מִ⁠כֶּֽם
25.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Because of your sins, Yahweh has kept these good things away from you]

25.q: עֲוֺנוֹתֵי⁠כֶ֖ם הִטּוּ אֵ֑לֶּה וְ⁠חַטֹּ֣אותֵי⁠כֶ֔ם מָנְע֥וּ הַ⁠טּ֖וֹב מִ⁠כֶּֽם
25.note: Yahweh is speaking of the people’s **iniquities** and **sins** as if they were living things that could turn away good things and keep them back. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You have lost these things because of your iniquities, and you do not have the good because of your sins]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **iniquities** and **sins**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [The wicked things you have done … and the wrong ways you have acted]

The pronoun **these** refers to the rain and the harvest that Yahweh gives, which the previous verse describes. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [these rains and harvests]

Yahweh is using the adjective **good** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the good harvests]

26.note: The expression **are found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [For wicked ones exist among my people]

Yahweh is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [people who are wicked]

The pronoun **he** refers to any one of the **wicked ones** whom Yahweh has just mentioned. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [each wicked one watches like fowlers lying in wait]

The point of this comparison is that just as **fowlers** wait quietly in hiding to trap birds, so these wicked people wait for a chance to trap other people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [he waits in hiding to ambush people, just as bird hunters wait quietly in hiding to trap birds]

The term **fowlers** describes men who catch birds by setting traps for them. If your readers would not be familiar with what fowlers are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [bird trappers]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the way these people take advantage of others as if they were hunters who **set a snare** to **capture** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they lay plans to trap others; they take advantage of people]

27.q: כִּ⁠כְלוּב֙ מָ֣לֵא ע֔וֹף כֵּ֥ן בָּתֵּי⁠הֶ֖ם מְלֵאִ֣ים מִרְמָ֑ה
27.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a cage** is **full of birds** that a hunter has caught, so the houses of these people are full of what they have gained by cheating others. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as a hunter’s cage is filled with the birds he has trapped, so their houses are filled with what they have gained by cheating others]

Here, **deceit** represents the goods that these people have gained by deceiving others. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [full of goods gained by deceiving others]

The word translated as **thus** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [as a result, they grow large and become rich]

28.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the wealth that these people have gained as if it had made their bodies **fat** and **sleek**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They have grown wealthy and prosperous]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **fatherless one**. He means orphans in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the legal cause of any fatherless child]

Yahweh is using the adjective **needy** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [people who are in need]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [They do not plead the legal cause; they do not plead the legal cause of the fatherless one]

29.note: Yahweh is using **my soul** to represent himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [should I not avenge myself]

30.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **Desolation** and **horror**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [Something devastating and horrifying]

The terms **Desolation** and **horror** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Terrible devastation]

31.note: This could mean: (1) Here, **their hands** represents the priests’ own authority, so that they rule as they themselves choose. Alternate translation: [and the priests rule as they themselves decide] or (2) it represents the direction of the prophets, so that the priests rule as the prophets tell them to. Alternate translation: [and the priests rule as the prophets direct them] If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language.

31.q: וְ⁠עַמִּ֖⁠י אָ֣הֲבוּ כֵ֑ן וּ⁠מַֽה תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ לְ⁠אַחֲרִיתָֽ⁠הּ
31.note: Even though Yahweh is addressing the people directly, he speaks about them in the third person as **my people**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [and you, my people, love it so, but what will you do in the end]

Yahweh is using the question form to warn the people that they will have no one to help them when he judges them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [but you will have no one to help you when the end comes!]
